research.job_description_summary: Capgemini India hires fresh graduates mainly as Analyst and Senior Analyst. Secondary 2026 sources describe a game-based aptitude assessment, about 25 pseudocode and technical MCQs, a coding test (mainly for Senior Analyst), a technical interview and an HR interview. The official recruitment-process pages were located but not fetched.
limitations: Capgemini's official recruitment-process and technical-graduates pages were located but not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED; rounds come from two 2026 secondary sources and are labeled REPORTED.
The Analyst and Senior Analyst split (coding mainly for Senior Analyst) is from a JobRise guide (2026-02-11) and was not confirmed officially.

The freshershunt aggregate (2026-08-19) reports counts such as Tell me about yourself 54, project 25, questions for us 23, Why Capgemini 12, hobbies 11, OOPS 6. Counts are user-submitted estimates. Items it names without counts are recorded with times_reported 1.
JobRise states a number of candidates were consulted but does not attribute its lists to individuals, so those lists are used only as topic context (class D).
Package figures (Analyst 4 to 4.5 LPA, Senior Analyst 7 to 7.5 LPA, aggregate 3.8 to 4.25 LPA) disagree and were not used.
Aptitude items are original practice proxies for the game-based round, which cannot be reproduced in text.
Track-specific allocation is a proposed structure; the aggregate does not split reports by role.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.

questions.prompt: A train 150 m long passes a pole in 10 seconds. How long does it take to cross a 250 m platform?
questions.relevance_to_role: A 2026 guide describes a game-based aptitude assessment as the first stage; this item is a conventional aptitude proxy.
follow_ups: What is the speed in km/h?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial source that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://jobrise.io/en/blog/capgemini-interview-questions-freshers-2026/.

mcq.explanation: Speed = 15 m/s. Distance to cross = 150 + 250 = 400 m, so time = 400 / 15 = 26.67 s.

questions.prompt: Compare arrays and linked lists, and write the steps to reverse a linked list.
